short: Paired covert/overt ECoG word decoding (M04) was ahead in 2011; best-of-64-electrode accuracies, prompt-only covert labels and unstated fold nesting make its gains over 25% chance upper bounds.
position: The paper [@pei2011decoding] changes two components. Its use-time action (M04), covert repetition of the same 36 words that are also decoded overtly, recorded on clinical ECoG, was ahead of the 2011 field, where imagined speech was decoded from EEG and intracranial work used attempted or overt speech (Appendix). Its decoder (M06), one classifier per electrode with the best location reported, is standard for its time but departs from the joint multi-electrode input of earlier and later work. The overt result holds; the covert result rests on prompt-defined labels with no silence check and on the best of 47–64 electrodes, and selection inside the folds is not stated (M03), so the gains over 25% chance are upper bounds. Today the same paired design on high-density ECoG reaches 80.4% median imagined-syllable accuracy [@zhao2026neural], so this paper is a feasibility result, not a benchmark.
